stages.name: None yet
stages.desc: No securely dated Phoenician or Greek presence

stages.name: Phoenician homeland
stages.desc: Tyre, Sidon and Byblos on the Levantine coast

stages.name: Greek homeland
stages.desc: Euboea, Attica, Crete and the Aegean

states.name: Cyprus
timeline: Greek-speaking kingdoms, founded after the Bronze Age collapse, rule much of the island
Phoenicians rebuild the great temple at Kition for Astarte: Kition becomes a Tyrian town
Seven Cypriot kings submit to Sargon II of Assyria; his stele stands at Kition
states.untouched: No securely dated Phoenician or Greek presence yet

states.name: Lebanon
timeline: Tyre, Sidon and Byblos: Phoenician city-states trading across the eastern Mediterranean
Hiram I reigns at Tyre and makes it the leading Phoenician city
Euboean drinking cups reach Tyre: Greek contact with the Levant
Tyre and Sidon pay tribute to Ashurnasirpal II of Assyria
By legend, Elissa (Dido) flees Tyre and her brother Pygmalion for Africa
states.untouched: No securely dated Phoenician or Greek presence yet

states.name: Morocco
timeline: Amazigh (Berber) peoples; no foreign settlement yet
Phoenicians trade at Lixus on the Atlantic coast, a shrine Pliny thought older than Gadir's
states.untouched: No securely dated Phoenician or Greek presence yet

states.name: Spain
timeline: Late Bronze Age Iberia: the Tartessian world of the southwest, rich in silver and copper
Huelva: a deposit of Phoenician pottery with Greek, Cypriot and Sardinian wares; radiocarbon c. 930–830 BC, pottery dates c. 800 BC or later. Greek pots likely came in Phoenician hands
Gadir (Cádiz): the earliest Phoenician houses date to c. 820–800 BC. Ancient writers placed its foundation in 1104 BC
Phoenician settlements spread along the Málaga coast
states.untouched: No securely dated Phoenician or Greek presence yet

states.name: Tunisia
timeline: Libyan peoples of the coast; no foreign settlement yet
Utica: radiocarbon on grain from a Phoenician well, late 10th to 9th century BC. Ancient writers placed its foundation in 1101 BC
Carthage founded by Tyre, by Timaeus' date; radiocarbon gives c. 835–800 BC, the oldest pottery c. 760 BC
Euboean and Pithekoussan cups in Carthage's earliest layers, carried in Phoenician trade
states.untouched: No securely dated Phoenician or Greek presence yet

states.name: Greece
timeline: Euboea, Attica and the islands: a Greek-speaking world recovering from the Bronze Age collapse
Lefkandi in Euboea: a hero's burial rich in Near Eastern imports
Phoenician storage jars begin to reach Kommos on Crete's south coast
Phoenicians set up a shrine of three standing pillars at Kommos
Chalcis and Eretria in Euboea send settlers west to Pithekoussai
Greeks adapt the Phoenician alphabet
states.untouched: No securely dated Phoenician or Greek presence yet

states.name: Italy
timeline: Nuragic Sardinia, Villanovan Etruria and the peoples of Sicily and the south
Phoenician amphorae and metal traders at Sant'Imbenia, a Nuragic village in Sardinia
Euboean cups reach Veii in Etruria and Sant'Imbenia in Sardinia
Euboeans settle Pithekoussai on Ischia, with Phoenicians living among them
Phoenicians settle Sulcis on Sant'Antioco, off Sardinia
Greek colonies begin in Sicily: Naxos, then Syracuse
states.untouched: No securely dated Phoenician or Greek presence yet

states.name: Portugal
timeline: Late Bronze Age communities of the Atlantic coast
Phoenician pottery and traders reach the Tagus valley at Santarém and Lisbon
states.untouched: No securely dated Phoenician or Greek presence yet

states.name: Malta
timeline: Bronze Age farming communities
Phoenician tombs and a sanctuary at Tas-Silġ mark Phoenician settlement
states.untouched: No securely dated Phoenician or Greek presence yet

events.title: Tyre rises
events.text: Tyre, on its island off the Levantine coast, emerges as the leading Phoenician trading city.

events.title: Greek kings on Cyprus
events.text: Greek-speaking kingdoms such as Paphos, founded after the Bronze Age collapse, rule much of Cyprus.

events.title: Hiram of Tyre
events.text: King Hiram I reigns at Tyre; the Bible remembers him as Solomon's partner in trade.

events.title: Lefkandi burial
events.text: At Lefkandi in Euboea, a warrior and a woman are buried in a great hall with imported Near Eastern treasures.

events.title: Huelva estuary hoard
events.text: More than four hundred bronze weapons sunk in the Huelva estuary show a busy Atlantic Bronze Age port.

events.title: Utica's oldest well
events.text: Grain from a Phoenician well at Utica gives radiocarbon dates in the late 10th to 9th centuries BC.

events.title: The Huelva deposit
events.text: Cattle bones from a deposit of Phoenician and Greek pottery in central Huelva date to about 930–830 BC by radiocarbon.

events.title: Jars at Kommos
events.text: Phoenician storage jars begin to reach Kommos, a harbour on Crete's south coast.

events.title: Euboean cups at Tyre
events.text: Euboean drinking cups decorated with pendent semicircles reach Tyre.

events.title: Ithobaal of Tyre
events.text: Ithobaal I takes Tyre's throne; Josephus credits him with founding Auza in Libya.

events.title: Tribute to Assyria
events.text: Tyre, Sidon and Byblos send tribute to Ashurnasirpal II, whose army has reached the Mediterranean.

events.title: Kition
events.text: Phoenicians rebuild a great temple at Kition on Cyprus and dedicate it to Astarte.

events.title: La Rebanadilla
events.text: A Phoenician island trading post near Málaga gives radiocarbon dates in the late 9th century BC.

events.title: Sant'Imbenia
events.text: In a Nuragic village in Sardinia, local people trade metal with Phoenician merchants.

events.title: Carthage radiocarbon
events.text: Animal bones from Carthage's earliest layers give radiocarbon dates of about 835–800 BC.

events.title: Gadir's first houses
events.text: The earliest Phoenician houses under Cádiz's Teatro Cómico date to about 820–800 BC.

events.title: Carthage by tradition
events.text: Timaeus dates Carthage's foundation by Elissa of Tyre to 38 years before the first Olympiad: 814 BC.

events.title: Kommos shrine
events.text: Phoenicians set up a shrine of three standing stone pillars in a temple at Kommos.

events.title: The Nora stone
events.text: A Phoenician inscription at Nora names Sardinia for the first time.

events.title: Euboean cups at Veii
events.text: Euboean cups reach Veii, an Etruscan centre north of the Tiber.

events.title: Doña Blanca
events.text: Phoenicians build a walled town at Castillo de Doña Blanca, across the bay from Gadir.

events.title: First Olympiad
events.text: The traditional date of the first Olympic Games, the anchor of later Greek dating.

events.title: Pithekoussai
events.text: Euboeans from Chalcis and Eretria settle Ischia, the first Greek base in the west.

events.title: Santarém
events.text: Phoenician pottery reaches the Tagus valley at Santarém, in today's Portugal.

events.title: Sulcis
events.text: Phoenicians settle Sulcis on the island of Sant'Antioco, off southwest Sardinia.

events.title: Carthage's oldest pots
events.text: Carthage's oldest pottery, with Euboean cups among it, dates to about 760 BC by style.

events.title: Málaga coast
events.text: Phoenician settlements line the coast at Morro de Mezquitilla and Toscanos.

events.title: Phoenicians at Ischia
events.text: Semitic inscriptions on jars at Pithekoussai show Phoenicians living among the Greeks.

events.title: Greek alphabet
events.text: Greeks adapt the Phoenician letters, adding vowels; Euboea is an early home of the new script.

events.title: Lixus
events.text: Phoenicians trade at Lixus on Morocco's Atlantic coast; Pliny thought its shrine older than Gadir's.

events.title: El Carambolo
events.text: A sanctuary of Phoenician type near Seville serves Astarte and Baal.

events.title: Cumae
events.text: Euboeans from Pithekoussai found Cumae on the mainland opposite.

events.title: Naxos in Sicily
events.text: Chalcidians found Naxos, the first Greek colony on Sicily, by Thucydides' dating.

events.title: Syracuse
events.text: Corinthians found Syracuse in eastern Sicily.

events.title: Nestor's cup
events.text: A cup in a boy's grave at Pithekoussai carries one of the oldest Greek verse inscriptions.

events.title: Malta
events.text: Phoenician tombs and a sanctuary at Tas-Silġ mark settlement on Malta.

events.title: Motya
events.text: Phoenicians settle the small island of Motya off western Sicily.

events.title: Lisbon
events.text: Phoenician pottery appears on the hill above the Tagus where Lisbon now stands.

events.title: Sargon's stele
events.text: Seven kings of Cyprus submit to Sargon II of Assyria; his stele is set up at Kition.

events.title: Taras
events.text: Spartans found Taras in the heel of Italy.

chartNote: Share of the area of nine of today's countries, by the earliest securely dated foreign presence in each; regions are modern boundaries and one find can colour a whole country, so this is a simplification. Where radiocarbon and pottery dates disagree, the map follows the radiocarbon dates; the pottery-based chronology puts several arrivals up to a century later. Greek pottery carried by Phoenician ships (as at Huelva and Carthage) is not counted as Greek presence.
